description:
Immutable histogram definitions. Bounds are display and aggregation choices, NOT quality thresholds — nothing here says 50 ms is good or 0.05 loss is bad. They apply to valid interval values, never to lifetime averages, and are weighted by eligible duration in milliseconds so a long quiet interval counts for more than a short one.

Buckets are (-inf, b0], (b0, b1], ..., (bn, +inf), so weights.length === upperBounds.length + 1. Only identical definitionIds may be merged; two histograms with different bounds have no common refinement and combining them would invent data. Quantiles read off these are approximate bucket ranges, never point estimates, and the UI must label them as such.

Inputs outside the metric's legal domain are rejected before bucketing rather than clamped into an edge bucket: a loss ratio of 1.3 is a producer bug, and silently filing it under '<= 1' would hide it.

definitions.note: The first bucket is exactly zero — a measured zero is valid evidence and deserves its own bucket rather than being lumped with 'almost zero'. The last bucket, above 1, can only be reached by a rejected value and should therefore always be empty.
